headline: High risk of filesystem conflict and cascading misuse; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but non-zero due to shared file/MCP surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, while agent_b reads and writes shared skill files. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if either agent consumes the other's file output as trusted text. The pairwise interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a writes prompts or tool output into files that agent_b later parses as instructions
IF agent_b ingests shared skill files without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Disable automatic parsing of shared files as instructions
Add a provenance header to any exchanged file
Review one sample handoff before enabling automation

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, and task prompts; agent_b can read and write the filesystem. If they share a workspace, sensitive context from agent_a can flow into agent_b outputs or external calls. No direct evidence shows the shared workspace, so this is inferred and kept at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same directory or mounted workspace
IF agent_b forwards file contents into its own outputs or API calls
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Restrict agent_b to a read-only copy of inputs
Remove secrets from shared files before execution
Turn off any automatic file upload or sync step

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell commands, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b can read/write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. In a shared repo, both can mutate the same working tree and git state, which matches the rubric's dangerous overlap. Defaults are unsafe unless orchestration adds locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF no external lock or serialization is enforced around writes
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Add a file lock around git and filesystem writes
Run one agent at a time for mutating tasks
Make agent_b operate on copies only

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a's sandboxing explicitly routes analysis/build commands, and agent_b's skills 'reference each other and build on shared context.' That makes it plausible that agent_b will treat agent_a outputs as authoritative without verification. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly observed, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-generated summaries or files as inputs
IF no verification step checks agent_a outputs before downstream action
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream actions
Require agent_b to cite source files for every claim
Compare agent_a outputs against a second source
Disable auto-execution of agent_a recommendations

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the visible data classes are non-regulated: agent_a handles code and task prompts, while agent_b handles marketing content. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a small compliance gap is plausible from shared handling practices. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise handling, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the shared workspace
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two runtimes
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention settings for both agents
Use separate storage buckets
Review logs for sensitive fields
